title: Salary Calculator Melbourne: Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Use our salary calculator Melbourne to turn your hourly rate into annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. Includes tax, Medicare, super, and minimum wage info.
salarySummary: Annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by hours per week (assumed 38 for full-time) times 52 weeks.

faqs.q: How do I use the salary calculator Melbourne?
faqs.a: Enter your base hourly rate into the calculator. If you are a casual employee, tick the 25% casual loading checkbox – do not add the loading to your rate yourself. The calculator then shows your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay based on 38 hours per week. It also estimates tax (using 2026–27 resident rates and the Medicare levy) and superannuation at 12% on top of your ordinary earnings.

faqs.q: What is the difference between annual salary and hourly rate?
faqs.a: An annual salary is a fixed amount paid over a year, usually for a set number of hours per week. An hourly rate is paid per hour worked. To compare, multiply your hourly rate by your weekly hours and by 52. For full-time work, we assume 38 hours per week. Remember that salary often includes paid leave, while hourly employees may receive casual loading or penalty rates. The calculator gives an estimate – your actual pay may vary due to overtime, allowances, or salary packaging.

faqs.q: Does the calculator include super and tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The calculator estimates tax using the 2026–27 resident tax brackets and the Medicare levy (2% with the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds). Super is estimated at 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your gross pay, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. It does not deduct HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary sacrifice amounts. Always check with the Australian Taxation Office or a tax professional for your exact situation.

bodyMarkdown:
## How the Salary Calculator Melbourne Works

If you are paid by the hour or have a salary offer, the [salary calculator Melbourne](/topics/hourly-conversion) helps you see the bigger picture. It converts your hourly rate into annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures so you can compare jobs, budget, or check your pay. The calculator assumes a standard 38-hour week for full-time work, but you can adjust the hours if your situation is different.

Simply type your base hourly rate. If you are a casual employee, tick the 25% casual loading checkbox – the calculator adds the loading on top. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading. The result shows your gross pay before tax and super, plus an estimate of tax and super.

## From Hourly to Annual: The Formula

The core formula is simple: annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a full-time employee on 38 hours, that is hourly × 38 × 52. For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. That gives $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44 per year (before tax). If you are casual, the minimum is $33.05 per hour including 25% loading, so $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,306.80 annually.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Your weekly pay is hourly × hours per week. Fortnightly is simply weekly × 2. For the minimum wage, weekly is $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.90, and fortnightly is $2,009.80. Many employers pay fortnightly, so this figure is handy for budgeting.

### What the Formula Does Not Include

The annual figure assumes you work the same hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It is a gross estimate. Your actual take-home pay depends on tax, super, and any deductions.

## Tax and Medicare on Your Annual Pay

The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator uses the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy. For 2026–27, the tax-free threshold is $18,200. Above that, you pay 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% from $45,001 to $135,000, 37% from $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income, but low-income earners may get a reduction. The calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide.

### Example: Minimum Wage Tax

For a full-time employee on the National Minimum Wage ($52,245.44 annual):
- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on next $26,800 ($18,201 to $45,000): 15% = $4,020
- Tax on remaining $7,245.44 ($45,001 to $52,245.44): 30% = $2,173.63
- Total tax: $6,193.63
- Medicare levy (2% of $52,245.44): $1,044.91
- Total tax and Medicare: $7,238.54
- Net annual pay: $45,006.90 (approximately $865.52 per week)

Remember, this is an estimate. Your actual tax may differ if you have deductions, offsets, or other income.

## Understanding the National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is set by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour for full-time and part-time employees, and $33.05 per hour for casuals (including 25% loading). However, many jobs are covered by awards or enterprise agreements that pay more. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page has details. If you are on an award, your minimum rate may be higher than the national minimum. The calculator does not know your award – it uses the rate you enter.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees get a 25% loading on top of the base rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. The calculator has a checkbox to add this loading. Do not manually add it to your rate. If you are a casual, tick the box and enter your base hourly rate (the rate before loading).

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation is a compulsory contribution from your employer, currently 12% of your ordinary earnings. It is paid on top of your gross pay, not deducted from it. The calculator estimates super at 12% of your annual gross pay, but only up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27). If your annual pay exceeds that, super is capped. For example, on the minimum wage, super would be 12% of $52,245.44 = $6,269.45 per year. This goes into your super fund, not your pocket.

## Using the Calculator for Fortnightly Pay

Many Australian employers pay fortnightly. The calculator shows your fortnightly gross pay (weekly × 2) and the estimated tax and super for that period. This helps you compare your pay slip with the estimate. Remember, tax is withheld each pay period based on your annual projected income, so the fortnightly tax figure is an approximation.

### Average Weekly Earnings Comparison

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports Average Weekly Earnings. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week, and all employees total earnings (including part-time) were $1,579.20 per week. These are averages across all industries and states, not medians for a specific job. Your pay may be higher or lower depending on your role, experience, and location. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page has more details.

## Important Disclaimer

This salary calculator Melbourne is a guide only. Annual pay is hourly rate × hours per week × 52, assuming the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. Always check with the Fair Work Ombudsman, Australian Taxation Office, or a qualified professional for your specific circumstances.

For more details, see the [reference tables](/data) or [pay guides](/blog).
